sentence: Ezetimibe is a prescribed cholesterol-lowering medicine that works by reducing how much cholesterol the gut absorbs.

sentence: It is used on its own when a statin cannot be taken or has not worked, and it can also be added to a statin.
note: NHS: prescribed if you cannot take statins or a statin does not work; can be used alongside statins.

sentence: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, or yellowing of the skin or eyes, needs a doctor or NHS 111 straight away.

sentence: NICE technology appraisal TA385 describes it as an option for primary (heterozygous-familial or non-familial) hypercholesterolaemia in adults, alone when a statin is contraindicated or not tolerated, or added to a statin when cholesterol remains inadequately controlled.

sentence: Heart UK says ezetimibe partly blocks the absorption of cholesterol in the small intestine.
Research reviews describe it as acting on a protein called NPC1L1 in the lining of the small intestine, which helps move cholesterol from the gut into the body.
note: Review: ezetimibe acts by inhibiting NPC1L1, the intestinal sterol uptake protein in the brush border (exact steps still debated).

sentence: Heart UK says ezetimibe works in a different way from statins, and that the two are often combined because their effects add up.
The NHS says ezetimibe usually lowers cholesterol levels within 2 weeks.
If it is stopped without another treatment, the NHS says cholesterol may go up again.
note: NHS: if you stop, cholesterol may rise again.

sentence: Stomach pain and diarrhoea are common side effects, and the NHS also lists extra wind and tiredness.
The NHS says these common side effects affect more than 1 in 100 people.
note: NHS: common side effects more than 1 in 100.

sentence: When ezetimibe is taken with a statin, Heart UK lists muscle pain, headaches and moderately raised liver enzymes among the most common effects.

sentence: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness or cramps are listed by the NHS as serious side effects, and the NHS advises contacting a doctor or NHS 111 straight away.

sentence: The NHS says it may be prescribed to people who cannot take statins, or for whom a statin has not worked.
It can also be prescribed together with a statin to lower cholesterol further.

NICE technology appraisal TA385 recommends ezetimibe on its own as an option for adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia, which includes familial and non-familial types, when a statin is contraindicated or not tolerated.

The same guidance allows it to be added to a statin when cholesterol remains inadequately controlled despite adjusting the statin dose, or when the dose is limited by intolerance, and a change to a different statin is being considered.

NICE guideline NG238 also covers ezetimibe for adults when statins are contraindicated or, after documented discussion of the strategies in the guideline, the person cannot tolerate statins of any intensity or dose.
